evidence.section: Mechanical Properties of Powders and Billets
evidence.quote: This can be explained by the formation of a cellular structure in the aluminum matrix and grain refinement during extrusion [14].

Oxid e films present on powder particles are refined in the extrusion process and distributed along fiber boundaries, providing hardening particles (quasicrystals and intermetallics), promoting higher hardness of the rods compared to the starting powder, and retarding recrystallization during annealing and heating.

Strain hardening proceeds in two stages. Its rate is very high at the first stage and lower at the second; the strain hardening of rods from the water-atomized powder is greater at both stages compared to rods from the gas-atomized powder.
Based on the above, we chose Al–8Cr–1.5Fe alloy composition for studies.
Two methods were used to produce the Al–8Cr–1.5Fe alloy powder to compare their effectiveness: melt atomization with inert gas and with water.
